chunks: And Ayatullah Sayyid Bahr al-Ulum said in his Rijali Fawa'id:

The Sheikh of the eminent Sheikhs and head of the leaders of the community, the opener of the doors of research through the establishment of proofs, and the crusher — through the eloquent outpourings of his articulate elucidation — of the arguments of the misguided sects,

In him were gathered the noble qualities of excellence; to him ended the leadership of all; and all agreed upon his knowledge, his virtue, his fiqh, his uprightness ('adala), his reliability (thiqa), and his grandeur.

He was — may Allah be pleased with him — of abundant virtues and plentiful noble merits, sharp of thought, subtle in discernment, ready with answers, ample in transmission, and an expert in rijal (narrator biography), historical reports, and poetry.
He was the most reliable of the people of his era in hadith and the most knowledgeable of them in fiqh and kalam; and every scholar who came after him benefited from him…

key_terms.الْجِلَّةِ: the eminent, the distinguished — honorific rijal descriptor (plural of جَلِيل)
key_terms.ثِقَتِهِ: his reliability (thiqa) — the core rijal evaluation term for trustworthy transmission
key_terms.خِلَالُ: noble qualities, virtuous characteristics (plural of خُلَّة)
key_terms.شَقَاشِقُ: rhetorical outpourings, eloquent oratorical force (plural of شِقْشِقَة)

ai.seo_question: What did Sayyid Bahr al-Ulum say in his Fawa'id al-Rijalliyya about the hadith reliability, fiqh mastery, and scholarly authority of the scholar eulogised in Chapter 12 of Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: This passage is a citation by Ayatullah Sayyid Bahr al-Ulum from his biographical compendium Fawa'id al-Rijalliyya, offering a comprehensive eulogy of a preeminent Shia scholar — widely identified as Sheikh al-Tusi — extolling his unrivalled mastery of hadith, fiqh, and kalam, and his standing as the most reliable narrator of his era. The praise highlights his intellectual acuity, his rhetorical power in refuting misguided sects, the unanimous scholarly consensus regarding his thiqa ('adala, reliability), and the universal benefit his legacy conferred on every subsequent generation of scholars.
